summary: The instruction, manual HC-4, README and visible package together fix every graded figure. The two figures the manual leaves open (a survey below three quarters of its shift, and the counted level of a reading above 115 dBA) are resolved by the explicit 'keep today's step, fed from the manual's figures' rule, and the current step is visible in shift.py and runs.py. I hand-traced the sealed expectations and they match this contract. No hidden convention, contradiction or representation-only grading was found.
checks_performed: Mapped each graded key (survey, id, group, dose, twa, status, ceiling, impulse, list orders) to its authority in instruction.md:5, README.md:29-41 and manual 1.2, 2.x, 3.x, 4.1, 5.x and 6.1.

Hand-traced below_three_quarters.jsonl (X1, X2, X3, Y1-Y6, V1, V2) through the kept shift.py step: sampled==0 gives 0, sampled<480 gives measured*480/sampled, otherwise measured. Sampled time was the manual's (readings >= 40.0 dBA) and measured dose used 85/3. All values matched.
Hand-traced above_ceiling.jsonl (Y1, Z1, Z2, K1) with the kept min(level, 115) counted level, 2.5/3.3 projection and 6.1 group mean. All values matched.

Hand-traced partial/whole/three_quarters/paused/sampled_time/threshold/twa/status/groups/quiet_members rows against manual 2.2-2.5, 3.1-3.3, 4.1, 5.3 and 6.1. Spot values matched, e.g. A3 twa 53.3, B2 377.976, S2 50.0/82.0/action, Y2 100.0/85.0/action.
Checked that the differential pairs vary only fields that the kept step ignores (shift_minutes below 3/4, or an above-ceiling vs 115.0 run), so equality of doses follows from the visible contract.
Checked TWA rounding exposure: no sealed TWA sits near an x.x5 boundary (the closest traced were 84.9549 and 81.9855), so half-up and round() cannot diverge on graded data.
Checked the dose tolerance: sealed 12-significant-figure doses (at most 5e-12 relative) plus the instruction's 1e-11 accept bound stay inside the verifier's 5e-11 midpoint.
Checked the driver byte-identity requirement (instruction.md:1) against test_outputs.py:70-78 and 384-387 and test.sh:22-26.
Checked the relabel transform (test_outputs.py:339-358). New names and ids, a worker shuffle and splitting each run at its own level leave every manual-defined figure unchanged.
Confirmed that the tests/shipped files are byte-identical in content to environment/app files (manifest hashes equal; read both).

coverage_sweep.category: Every grading rule has a candidate-visible authority
coverage_sweep.reason: Criterion/exchange (3.1), threshold inclusive (2.3), sampled time over readings >= 40.0 (2.2, 2.4), partial definition (2.5), projection to own shift and whole-shift rule (3.3), TWA formula (4.1), half-up tenth rounding with status judged on the reported TWA (1.2), bands 82.0/85.0 with flagged workers over (5.3), ceiling > 115.0 (5.1), impulse >= 140.0 (2.6, 5.2), group plain mean with no flags (6.1), group order (README:39-41). Uncovered figures are resolved by instruction.md:3 plus visible shift.py:17-22 and runs.py:18-23.

coverage_sweep.category: Input domain and needed boundaries specified
coverage_sweep.reason: Manual 1.4 fixes the domain, and instruction.md:3 marks out-of-domain inputs as open. within_limits (test_outputs.py:143-155) keeps every graded survey inside 1.4. Graded boundaries (79.9/80.0/80.1, 115.0/115.1, 139.9/140.0, exactly 3/4, exactly whole shift, 82.0/85.0 rounded TWAs, empty log, 0.0 runs) each have a manual rule or the explicit keep-today rule.

coverage_sweep.category: Rendered instruction, declared artifacts and verifier paths agree
coverage_sweep.reason: The instruction names /app/src, /app/tools/noisedose_run.py and the command. The verifier runs python3 -I -S on the verifier's driver copy against delivered /app/src and byte-checks the delivered driver. task.toml artifacts is /app/. No broken template text or test sentinels were found.
The example survey is illustrative input only; the verifier does not grade it and it does not contradict the manual. The instruction says rules hold beyond it.

Group order is ASCII with digits before letters (README:39-40, report_order.jsonl). Rounding direction is stated. The kept 480-minute scaling and 115 dBA counted level are visible in the shipped code, and the instruction points to them. No other convention is needed by the sealed expectations.

JSON is parsed. Extra worker and top-level keys are ignored. An integral twa is accepted as a number, and dose is graded by tolerance. Group rows are rejected if they carry ceiling/impulse keys, which manual 6.1 ('a group carries no ceiling or impulse flag') and the README group key list support. Booleans and strings compare by exact type, as the README types require.

The instruction's stated comparisons (exact for labels, flags, status, order and twa tenth; the dose accept bound of 1e-11 and reject bound of 1e-10) match the verifier (REL/ABS 5e-11, exact twa, exact types). The verifier grades only families inside the instruction's announced workload.

'Add no exception, clamp or guard the manual does not give' does not conflict with keeping today's min(level, CEILING) and the 480 scaling, because those are kept, not added. The requirement to leave the driver unchanged is achievable. The candidate environment has no third-party dependencies, and -I -S execution only needs the stdlib package.
